[Rating: 1/10] Ugh, never again.  There's just so much that's so situational- am I going to be the one who has to spend the three AP on forcing a trade that's beneficial to both players because of the way the turn order falls on a scoring round?  Am I going to have 10 pieces at one end of the board that can't do shit because I get sniped?  Am I going to get really lucky and draw two of the sime treasure in a row?  Am I going to draw a blatantly worse tile than the previous person?  I can't control any of it, so why does this take ninety fucking minutes?

Yes, many options will cause a game more often then not to be more strategical, but I rather have games where you can do just a couple of things that make it a really hard choice of what you want to do. [Rating: 1/10] Played a long time ago. Did not want to play because I found the premise incompatible with modern archaeology.

[Rating: 1/10] It's not bad, and I like building the landscape, but it feels so awkward competing/interacting on this map. I can't help but think it's Mexica but less interesting in every way. And way less immersive where you just charge through the map to grab up victory points before someone else, and then it's empty again. The 10 AP is kind of ridiculous haha.  Thinking too much about this, how SO many eurogames are about claiming something and jealously chasing off others who might interact. But not violently, only with passive-aggression. It's depressing.

[Rating: 1/10] Classic K&K area control game, considering picking up a copy but worry it's too long and random for what it is. Very plain area control game, the AP system and how that relates to logistical puzzle is really the only thing that stands out about it otherwise it's a pretty forgettable experience despite all the player interaction. [Rating: 2/10] 2-4 players, about 2 hours.  I find this game very dry - I thought the exploration would be much more fun.  Spending 10 action points each turn is not a mechanic I will be searching out for future gaming experiences.

[Rating: 2/10] Update: Four player games are much more interesting. Not sure if the artifacts are worthwhile.  I have only played two player, but believe it is broken for two.  There are three possible strategies in the game: Either build up temples, search for treasure, or a comination of both.  In a two player game, these choices are reduced mere randomness of the tiles/treasures drawn due to the zero-sum nature of the game (game theory). [Rating: 2/10] Desperately wants to feel sandbox-y and open/vast but is significantly more constraint than it appears at a glance. AP system is neat, though, and simple tile rotation (and opponent placement) can create interesting chokepoints. A decent game, bordering on filler but with a bit more oomph, could see this getting old quickly or if played in rapid succession.
